note: No official English version exists for any of these plans, so the English here is our translation unless a plan says otherwise. Each target keeps the original Chinese wording and the article it comes from.

series.title: Beijing
series.summary: Three plans in four years. The headline measure moves from revenue, to firm and product counts, to hardware, compute, data and parts specs; units differ between versions, so only the direction compares.

series.title: National robot industry plans
series.summary: From Made in China 2025’s qualitative goals to unit and market-share targets (2016), then growth and density targets (2021, 2023).

series.title: National humanoid and embodied-AI
series.summary: The 2023 humanoid guidance names firm goals without counts; the 15th Five-Year Plan names embodied intelligence without a number; 2026 adds standards and real-world training.

series.title: Shanghai
series.summary: The only plan here with a detailed money schedule.

series.title: Shenzhen
series.summary: The 2026 revision keeps every numeric target; only two tasks were reworded.

plans.title_en: Beijing Embodied-AI Robot Industry High-Quality Development Action Plan (2026-2028)

plans.issuer_en: Beijing Municipal Bureau of Economy and Information Technology
changes: Versus Beijing 2025–27: Firm target tightens from >=50 core chain firms to a named tier: >=5 internationally first-class + 10 domestic-leading humanoid makers plus >=200 SME/high-tech firms. Output goes from '>10,000 units total scale (2027)' to '200,000 units/yr capacity in Beijing (2028)' (capacity vs production, not like-for-like). Data goal changes unit from a ten-million-item dataset to >1,000,000 hours from >=100 real scenarios. New in 2026: >50,000 PFlops compute, BTH 25% of national whole-robot capacity, >60% key-part supporting rate, component specs (e.g. motor 60 N·m/kg, reducer 15,000 h, dexterous hand under RMB 10,000), 8/30/70 standards, 100 university teams, safety-governance programme ('one machine, one code'). Dropped: the 'RMB 100bn-class cluster' wording and the 'at least 100 scaled applications' count (replaced by 50 benchmark scenarios + 15 solutions).

Versus Beijing 2023–25: From a revenue target (core robot industry >RMB 30bn by 2025, 100 products, 100 scenarios) to hardware, compute, data and parts-localization targets; no revenue target in 2026.

us_comparison.china: Output targets: Beijing 200,000 whole robots/yr capacity by 2028 (BTH 25% of national capacity); Beijing >10,000-unit scale by 2027; Shanghai core industry >RMB 50bn by 2027; Hangzhou whole-robot firms >RMB 20bn by 2027; Shenzhen associated industry >RMB 100bn; national 2016 plan 100,000 domestic industrial robots/yr (2020).
us_comparison.us: No federal output, capacity or revenue target for robots or humanoids found. Closest: H.R. 7334 (introduced 2026-02-03), which would only create a study commission.
us_comparison.note: No federal target. The bill sets no number and contains no appropriation (text searched for appropriation authority; none beyond 'appropriate congressional committees'). Status of the bill after introduction not verified.

us_comparison.china: Beijing: >=5 internationally leading + 10 domestic-leading humanoid makers by 2028 (earlier: >=50 core chain firms, 2027); national humanoid guidance 2-3 globally influential firms by 2025; Shenzhen 10 firms >RMB 10bn valuation.
us_comparison.us: No federal target for number of leading robot firms.
us_comparison.note: No federal target (the commission bill is the only federal robotics-specific vehicle located).

us_comparison.china: Beijing: >50,000 PFlops new embodied-AI dedicated compute clusters (precision unspecified) plus compute pairing; Shanghai compute vouchers up to RMB 40m/yr per firm; Shenzhen training-compute vouchers.
us_comparison.us: No robotics-specific federal compute target. DOE Genesis Mission consortium has a working group on 'high-performance computing and cloud infrastructure' and one on 'robotics and automation', but sets no compute number for robots.
us_comparison.note: Not comparable: Genesis is an AI-for-science platform; the quote only shows overlapping working-group topics. No federal compute target for embodied AI.

us_comparison.china: Beijing: national embodied-AI data infrastructure, >1,000,000 hours of data from >=100 real scenarios by 2028 (2025 plan: ten-million-item dataset); Shanghai corpus platform and corpus vouchers up to RMB 5m/yr; Hangzhou data-purchase subsidy up to RMB 300k.
us_comparison.us: No federal embodied-AI training-data target found. Genesis consortium working group on 'data integration and standards' is the closest topical overlap (science data, not robot demonstration data).
us_comparison.note: No federal target; do not equate. Units differ anyway (hours vs items).

us_comparison.china: Mostly caps, not totals: Shanghai up to 30%/RMB 50m R&D, RMB 20m platforms, RMB 10m demos; Guangdong up to RMB 50m national manufacturing-innovation centre; Beijing up to RMB 100m per project (press conference, measures in preparation); Beijing 2026 plan gives no amount but cites government guidance funds; no plan states a total budget.
us_comparison.us: NSF National Robotics Initiative (sunset 2022; succeeded by FRR which publishes no total): over $250 million in 12 years across multi-agency partners. ARM Institute (Manufacturing USA, DoD): $80 million federal at founding in 2017, with $173 million non-federal. ($250M+ over ~12 years (NRI); $80M federal (ARM 2017 founding))
us_comparison.note: Different instruments and scales: Chinese plans cap per-project support, US figures are programme totals over a decade. A like-for-like annual comparison cannot be made from these sources; later ARM/DoD awards (reported ~$87-90M AFRL) were not verified to a primary source.

us_comparison.china: Beijing: Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei key-component supporting rate >60% by 2028; spec targets for motors, reducers, sensors, hands; Shenzhen/Guangdong support domestic chips; 2016 plan 50% domestic share of key components.
us_comparison.us: No federal localisation target. Trade measure only: Section 232 proclamation of 2026-10-28 directs negotiations on robotics, industrial machinery and components imports; no tariff set in the proclamation text read.
us_comparison.note: A trade action, not a domestic-content or localisation target; the proclamation text defers to negotiations and a 180-day update.

us_comparison.china: Beijing: 20 industrial + 20 service + 10 special benchmark scenarios, 15 scalable solutions; Hangzhou 30 demo scenarios (100 scenarios built); Shanghai 100 scenarios; MIIT/SASAC 2026: 100+ high-value scenarios, ~10,000-unit-class deployment capability; Robot+ 2023: 200 scenarios.
us_comparison.us: No federal deployment or scenario-count target for robots.
us_comparison.note: No federal target. FY2026 NDAA Section 225 (Army robotic automation in munitions manufacturing) exists in the site's policy corpus but was not re-verified here, so it is not used as a counterpart.

us_comparison.china: Beijing: lead/participate in 8 international, 30 national, 70 industry/group standards; MIIT/TC8 first humanoid and embodied-AI standards system (2026 edition, 6 parts).
us_comparison.us: No federal standards-count target found. Not exhaustively searched: NIST robot test methods and ANSI/A3 standards were not examined.
us_comparison.note: Unverified negative; only the bill text was checked.

us_comparison.china: Executive-level action: China has MIIT guidance (2023), a 15th Five-Year Plan named column for embodied intelligence (2026) and MIIT/SASAC deployment action (2026-06).
us_comparison.us: No signed national robotics strategy or robotics-specific executive order found. A robotics executive order was reported as under consideration for 2026 (Politico via secondary sites, not fetchable here: HTTP 403). The signed action located is a Section 232 trade proclamation (2026-10-28).
us_comparison.note: The 'under consideration' report is secondary and unverified here; absence of an order is based on search only, not an exhaustive review of the Federal Register.

caveats: Quotes marked secondary are from news reports of a document; the document text itself was not read.

PDF/web-extracted Chinese quotes have whitespace removed (extraction inserted spaces inside numbers); characters otherwise verbatim and machine-verified as substrings of the saved source files in this directory.
English text_en fields and all translations are ours unless a plan's 'translation' says otherwise; no official English version was found for any plan except where noted (none).

Beijing 2023 robotics plan: official final text page not found; primary text is the April 2023 consultation draft; final headline figures come from Xinhua. Beijing 2025 embodied-AI plan text is the file on the Beijing Science & Technology Commission consultation path; its figures match the 2025-02-28 press conference but it may not be the issued text.

Units ambiguous: Beijing 2025-2027 '量产总规模率先突破万台' (cumulative vs annual); Beijing 2026 '20万台/年整机生产能力' (capacity, not sales; humanoid-only not stated); '50000PFlops' (numeric precision unspecified); '千万条' data items vs '100万小时'; MIIT/SASAC '万台级' (order of 10,000, English report says 10,000).
No plan examined states a total budget in yuan. Every money figure found is a per-project or per-firm cap, a subsidy rate, or a fund named without size.

Not found or not fetched: Beijing humanoid innovation center plans; Beijing 2026 plan '一图读懂' explainer; Jiangsu, Nanjing, Dongguan, Foshan, Tianjin, Zhejiang provincial plans (search-summary only); national venture guidance fund primary text; Tianjin; 2015 MIC2025 robotics technology roadmap; Shenzhen revised-edition official page (403).
Search-engine summaries were used only to find documents; no figure in plans.json relies on a summary alone.

Document numbers or dates taken from search summaries and not re-read on a primary page: Shenzhen revised edition issue date 2026-06-18; MIIT/SASAC notice number; 2016 plan signing date; Beijing 2023 issue date 2023-06-28.
